svg.title: Three firms that faced conflicting demands from two governments
svg.desc: Diagram of three rows, each with a firm, shown by its logo, between two governments. Microsoft: the United States in 2013 demanded emails stored in Ireland, and European Union privacy law restricts sending data abroad. ByteDance: the United States in 2020 said to sell TikTok's U.S. business or leave the market, and China in 2020 said no export of the algorithm without a license. DiDi: a United States law of 2020 said to let U.S. inspectors review audits or be delisted, and China in 2021 treated the firm's data as a matter of national security.
svg.text: The firm's data is a matter
